title: An essential convex hull criterion for false confidence in location models
description:
Unrefereed research candidate. Balch, Martin and Ferson (2019) showed that for any additive probability produced from data, some false hypotheses tend to receive high probability, a phenomenon they called false confidence. Martin (2024) asked which hypotheses are affected. This candidate answers that question exactly for flat-prior posteriors in location models with radially decreasing errors.

Hull criterion. Let CH be the closed convex hull of the essential support of a hypothesis H. For exponential-power errors with p>1, including the Gaussian case, H is valid at every threshold at a parameter exactly when that parameter is not in the interior of CH. For a radial density g with tail probability S, this equivalence holds for all hypotheses if and only if liminf S(R)/g(R-b)=0 for every b>0. Tails like exp(-r log r) satisfy this in dimension one and fail it in every higher dimension.

Complements and marginals. A hypothesis and its complement are both globally valid only if the hypothesis is almost everywhere a halfspace. This corrects, in these models, a conjecture of Martin (2024): a ball is non-linear yet valid at every false parameter. The posterior of a real function is exactly calibrated at every parameter if and only if its sublevel sets are almost everywhere parallel halfspaces, that is, the function is a strictly monotone function of one linear form.

High confidence at a fixed level. All-threshold failure may occur only at low thresholds, so the hull criterion alone says nothing about 95% confidence: (-2,-1) union (1,2) in the standard Gaussian model never receives posterior mass above 0.39. With log-concave errors, if a closed convex set contains the complement of H and has posterior mass at most s<1/2 when the observation equals the truth, then H receives posterior probability at least 1-s with sampling probability at least one half. In a worked satellite conjunction example with sigma/R=10, a certain collision produces a computed collision probability of at most 0.01 with probability one.

Prior work and limits: the sufficient direction is elementary, halfspace validity is in Martin (2023), and the Gaussian converse combines classical Laplace-transform growth with a tail comparison. The model assumes known shape and exact matching of sampling and posterior error laws. The prior-art finding is a record of dated searches, not proof of priority. The archive contains the manuscript (PDF and Markdown source), three deterministic check scripts with retained output, the figure code and SHA-256 sums. Assurance: written proofs; internal AI-assisted review only (not human peer review, independent reproduction or proof-assistant verification). Creator: Anonymous. Text CC0-1.0; code MIT.
